title: The shortest UK pub crawl
hook: Mathematicians proved the shortest route visiting nearly 50,000 UK pubs.
peek: In 2018 a team led by William Cook found the shortest possible walk visiting almost every pub in the United Kingdom, and then proved no shorter one exists. It was a showcase for the travelling salesman problem, one of maths' most famous hard puzzles.
lede: The travelling salesman problem asks for the shortest round trip through a list of places. It sounds easy, yet no one knows a fast method that always works for big lists. In 2018 the mathematician William Cook and colleagues solved it for 49,687 pubs across the United Kingdom, finding a tour of roughly 64,000 kilometres and proving it is the shortest.

bullets.text: The number of possible tours explodes. Even 20 stops allow more than 60 million billion different round trips, so checking them one by one is hopeless for 50,000 pubs.

Cook's team used Concorde, a program built for this problem. It finds a very good tour, then uses linear programming to prove a lower limit on any tour's length. When the two meet, the route is proven best.
The method traces back to 1954, when George Dantzig, Ray Fulkerson and Selmer Johnson solved a tour of 49 American cities by hand-guided calculation, a record at the time.
The 2018 route followed a 2016 effort by the same team covering about 24,700 pubs. The longer list mapped the pubs of the UK almost completely.

Fast routes save money for delivery vans, circuit-board drilling and telescope scheduling. Finding a method that always solves such problems quickly is tied to the P versus NP question, a $1 million Millennium Prize problem.
